{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "Feasible as a controlled single-column ELM sensitivity experiment varying soil clay fraction while holding forcing, location, and all other parameters fixed.",
    "answerable": [
      "How the surface runoff vs. drainage/recharge partitioning of infiltrating water shifts as clay content increases from 5% to 55%",
      "Sensitivity of infiltration capacity, soil moisture storage, and evapotranspiration to clay-driven changes in hydraulic conductivity and porosity",
      "Monotonic trend and approximate threshold behavior in runoff ratio across the clay gradient"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Lateral/hillslope runoff routing between columns (single-column has no lateral connectivity)",
      "Real-site validation without site-specific soil profile and flux observations",
      "Fine-scale preferential/macropore flow through clay soils (not represented in ELM's Richards/BGC hydrology)",
      "Long-term pedogenic feedbacks (texture is held static by design)"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "Six columns evenly span the requested 5%-55% clay range in ~10% increments (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55), enough to resolve the nonlinear runoff/recharge response and identify any threshold while keeping the ensemble small and interpretable. All columns share identical location and forcing so clay content is the sole varied factor.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "clay05", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "sand-loam mix, 5% clay, 55% sand, 40% silt"},
    {"id": "clay15", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "loam, 15% clay, 45% sand, 40% silt"},
    {"id": "clay25", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "clay-loam, 25% clay, 35% sand, 40% silt"},
    {"id": "clay35", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "clay-loam, 35% clay, 30% sand, 35% silt"},
    {"id": "clay45", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "silty-clay, 45% clay, 20% sand, 35% silt"},
    {"id": "clay55", "lat": 39.0, "lon": -96.5, "soil_texture": "clay, 55% clay, 15% sand, 30% silt"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1991",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2010",
    "STOP_N": "20",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1991-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER",
      "QDRAI",
      "QRGWL",
      "QINFL",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QFLX_EVAP_TOT",
      "QSOIL",
      "QVEGT",
      "H2OSOI",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "ZWT",
      "WA",
      "TSOI",
      "TWS"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "Single-point ELM (I-compartment) configuration with user-defined surface/soil dataset",
    "Ability to override PCT_CLAY (and complementary PCT_SAND) per soil layer in the surface dataset to set each clay level",
    "GSWP3 or CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing at the chosen point",
    "Spin-up capability (accelerated-decomposition + final spin-up) to equilibrate soil moisture/water table before the 20-yr analysis run"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Site is a temperate continental grassland (Konza-like, central Kansas) with identical vegetation/PFT across all columns; only soil texture differs",
    "Clay fraction is applied uniformly over the full soil column depth; sand and silt adjusted to sum to 100%",
    "ELM derives hydraulic properties (Ksat, porosity, matric potential, Clapp-Hornberger b) from texture via internal pedotransfer functions, so no direct override of hydraulic parameters is needed",
    "Runoff/recharge partitioning is diagnosed as QOVER (surface runoff) vs. QDRAI (subsurface drainage/recharge proxy) after model reaches quasi-steady state",
    "Each column spun up separately with its own texture before the common 1991-2010 analysis period; identical forcing, atmospheric CO2, and nitrogen deposition applied to all",
    "Default 10-15 layer ELM soil hydrology (Richards equation) with SIMTOP/VIC-style runoff scheme as configured by compset"
  ]
}

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as a controlled single-column ELM sensitivity experiment varying soil clay fraction while holding forcing, location, and all other parameters fixed.
answerable: How the surface runoff vs. drainage/recharge partitioning of infiltrating water shifts as clay content increases from 5% to 55%
Sensitivity of infiltration capacity, soil moisture storage, and evapotranspiration to clay-driven changes in hydraulic conductivity and porosity
Monotonic trend and approximate threshold behavior in runoff ratio across the clay gradient
not_answerable: Lateral/hillslope runoff routing between columns (single-column has no lateral connectivity)
Real-site validation without site-specific soil profile and flux observations
Fine-scale preferential/macropore flow through clay soils (not represented in ELM's Richards/BGC hydrology)
Long-term pedogenic feedbacks (texture is held static by design)

parsed.n_justification: Six columns evenly span the requested 5%-55% clay range in ~10% increments (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55), enough to resolve the nonlinear runoff/recharge response and identify any threshold while keeping the ensemble small and interpretable. All columns share identical location and forcing so clay content is the sole varied factor.
requires_capabilities: Single-point ELM (I-compartment) configuration with user-defined surface/soil dataset
Ability to override PCT_CLAY (and complementary PCT_SAND) per soil layer in the surface dataset to set each clay level
GSWP3 or CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing at the chosen point
Spin-up capability (accelerated-decomposition + final spin-up) to equilibrate soil moisture/water table before the 20-yr analysis run
assumptions: Site is a temperate continental grassland (Konza-like, central Kansas) with identical vegetation/PFT across all columns; only soil texture differs
Clay fraction is applied uniformly over the full soil column depth; sand and silt adjusted to sum to 100%
ELM derives hydraulic properties (Ksat, porosity, matric potential, Clapp-Hornberger b) from texture via internal pedotransfer functions, so no direct override of hydraulic parameters is needed
Runoff/recharge partitioning is diagnosed as QOVER (surface runoff) vs. QDRAI (subsurface drainage/recharge proxy) after model reaches quasi-steady state
Each column spun up separately with its own texture before the common 1991-2010 analysis period; identical forcing, atmospheric CO2, and nitrogen deposition applied to all
Default 10-15 layer ELM soil hydrology (Richards equation) with SIMTOP/VIC-style runoff scheme as configured by compset
